questions.stem: You share a lakehouse with a user who has no workspace role. They must query its tables through the SQL analytics endpoint and nothing more. What do you grant?

options.text: Build on the default semantic model only
Read plus Read all with SQL analytics endpoint
Read plus Read all with Apache Spark

questions.explanation: Sharing gives Read on the item. Adding Read all with SQL analytics endpoint lets the user query the tables through T-SQL; Read all with Apache Spark would also open the data to Spark.

questions.stem: A data scientist outside the workspace needs to read a lakehouse's files and tables from their own Spark notebooks. Which permission do you add when sharing the lakehouse?

options.text: Read all with SQL analytics endpoint

questions.explanation: The Spark permission gives access to the lakehouse's data in OneLake, which Spark reads directly.

questions.stem: You share a warehouse with a user and grant no extra permissions. What can they do?

options.text: Connect to the warehouse, but read only objects they've been granted access to with T-SQL
Nothing; sharing without extra permissions fails

questions.explanation: Read lets the user connect. Access to data then comes from the extra sharing permissions or from T-SQL GRANT statements on specific objects.

questions.stem: Which two statements about item-level sharing are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Shared items can't be read by groups
Sharing an item gives access to that item only, not to the rest of the workspace
Item sharing works only for reports
Item permissions can give someone less than any workspace role, such as only connecting to a shared warehouse
Sharing an item makes the user a workspace Viewer

questions.explanation: Item permissions apply to one item only. A plain share of a warehouse gives Read, which only lets the user connect, which is less than the Viewer role gives.
